title: Lesson Plan — School Kitchen Garden (Class 6 CBSE Vocational Education)
subject: Vocational Education
objectives: Define a kitchen garden and explain three benefits.
Identify a suitable spot and the right crop for the current season.
Name and use simple gardening tools safely.
Compare three ways to start a plant: direct sowing, seedlings, cuttings.
Describe daily / weekly care steps for plants.
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with plants from Class 5 EVS / Science.
An outdoor space or a few pots (preferable, not required).
materials: Real (or photograph of) khurpi, trowel, watering can, mulch
A small tray of seeds (spinach / coriander)
A few pots, soil and compost

activities.description: Hook: hold up a tomato. Ask 'where did this come from?' and 'could we grow this at school?'. Take guesses and promise the lesson will show how.
Walk to a possible garden spot at school. Students assess: Is it sunny? Is water nearby? Any heavy footfall? Sketch a quick plan in their notebook.
Cover four blocks: (i) what is a kitchen garden + planning; (ii) three Indian seasons + crop choices; (iii) tools and materials; (iv) sowing methods (direct, seedlings, cuttings) + care + harvesting.
teacher_actions: Sketch a sample bed on the board.
Display real tools and pass around.
Demonstrate direct sowing live with a tray of soil + a few seeds.
Drill the three seasons with examples.
student_actions: Try sowing one seed in a pot.
Repeat the names of the three seasons.

activities.description: Worksheet practice: 6 questions covering definition, season, tools, sowing, care, harvesting; plus a small garden plan to draw.
student_actions: Sketch a 5×5 m plan in pairs.

activities.description: Exit ticket: 4 questions, one from each block.
Homework: start a 'garden diary'. Find one plant at home or near school; observe it for a week and record what changes.

homework: Start a garden diary: pick one plant at home or near school. Record date, weather and one observation each day for 5 days.
Sketch a small kitchen-garden layout for your home (5–6 plants), labelling the season and each plant.
List 5 vegetables your family eats often and find out which season each is grown in.
assessment_ideas: Use the 4-item exit ticket as formative.
Run a 10-question quiz next class as summative.
Mark the LONG_ANSWER on planning a 5×5 m Rabi garden using the rubric in the answer key.
Peer-grade the garden diary at the end of one week.
references: NCERT Class 6 Vocational Education — Kaushal Bodh, Chapter 1: School Kitchen Garden.
